utterances.text: On the basis of the meetings that I personally have with General Kadijevic and his leadership and the two meetings that he had at the Presidency with his delegation, the JNA was Yugoslav and it did not interfere in political decisions and agreements on the fate of the future Yugoslavia. I have to remind you that US Secretary of State James Baker when on the 21st of June, 1991, when he landed in Belgrade he expressed his readiness to have Yugoslavia be preserved, but that certain transformations had to be carried out. Then the JNA was given this mandate to ensure this transformation by peaceful means as much as possible. He talked to Kucan, Milosevic, and Tudjman as he presented this concept of the preservation of Yugoslavia that would be a democratic community, if I can put it that way, of states and peoples. And this political pluralism had to be introduced in Yugoslavia after the League of Communists of Yugoslavia fell apart in January 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Doctor. I would like you to look at the following. Could I have counted on the support of the JNA for anything else but the preservation of Yugoslavia and did they count on our support in the preservation of Yugoslavia, mobilisations, and so on, you did know something about that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether they counted on your support, I cannot say, because none of them ever confirmed that to me, none of the members of the leadership or of the staff of the JNA. Let me also say straight away that in all the statements that were given and all the meetings, official and unofficial, with the JNA generals, none of them ever said that they would support the concept of the SDS or any national party, not even the concept that was advocated by Mr. Milosevic, that is to say, bringing tanks out into the streets of Belgrade on the 9th of March, 1991. So the JNA tried as much as possible, at least the leadership that I had contact with - now maybe you contacted some other generals or captains or others authorities - but my talks with the General Staff and the generals were only along the following lines of making a joint effort to ensure peace and the peaceful political transformation of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 67 you were asked about the statements of Biljana Plavsic and Professor Koljevic is there as well about the functioning of this multi-ethnic society. Did Mrs. Plavsic have a function in the Presidency that had to do with the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: She was president of the council for protecting the constitutional order of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When meeting her officially or privately, did you see whether she was pleased with how things were developing in terms of the protection of the constitutional order?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: Which constitutional order? Are you referring to Bosnia-Herzegovina or Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In general terms, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: I don't know about whether she was pleased or not, but I do have to remind you that it was precisely you, the national parties, that violated the constitutional provisions of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And in that way you violated all sorts of legal provisions. Mr. Karadzic, I have to remind you of this. The parliament of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you, you did not change a single law, man. You did not change the constitution. You did not pass any amendments to the constitution since you were given this mandate by the European community to set up a government, it was your duty to base your authority on the laws that existed before the elections because you didn't have any new laws. You violated all sorts of constitutional provisions. And therefore, if this is a question of responsibility then there is the responsibility for the way in which you ignored this through the Presidency, through the government, through the Assembly, all the laws that were still in force, including the election of Mr. Izetbegovic as president of the Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber how even the most ordinary decisions were reached in the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I'll do so very gladly. At the first session of the newly formed Assembly - and that was on the 22nd of December, 1990, and that lasted for two days - and during those two days you did not manage to reach agreement, not even on setting up an agenda. So you couldn't even agree on the agenda. At the end of that second day, Mr. Krajisnik suggested: People, let us at least elect this Presidency because nothing else seems to be working. And that's how the Presidency was elected. At the next session where I was elected, and that also lasted three days, no agreement was reached. And I could not even take an oath because again you were quarrelling about whether it was supposed to be in Cyrillic, whether it was supposed to include Yugoslavia, whether it should include Bosnia-Herzegovina as an integral part of Yugoslavia, and so on and so forth. So these were futile discussions, a waste of public money. And you could not agree on that at all. So this was a clear reflection of how these organs operated. The national parties brought that to my country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr. Zepinic. Do you know, do you remember, what the oath was on the basis of the law and who asked for what kind of changes -- actually, what did the Serbs ask for and what did the secessionists ask for?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: The Serbs asked for the formulation of Yugoslavia only and the Croats wanted "Yugoslavia" to be deleted and the Muslims asked for sort of half-half, if you understand what I'm saying. So these polemics reflected all of this at various meetings until war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, did the oath include "Yugoslavia" as such?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: Yes. According to the Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that was an integral part. So since you did not change the constitution, what right did you have to discuss any kind of change to the wording of the oath?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned today that I was more in favour of the environmental movement than nationalism. Do you remember which was the last national party to be established in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to dictate all the dates to you of all your Assemblies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, just give me the order, the sequence.

utterances.speaker: VITOMIR ZEPINIC
utterances.text: The SDA, the H -- actually, it was the HDZ that was first established. Then on the basis of the amendments to the Constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Croatian Community that was established by Mate Boban on the 27th of March could not be registered because it included part of the HDZ from Zagreb. So basically the HDZ, with its first president, Perinovic, was the last party that was registered but it was the first party to be established --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, unless you could conclude very shortly, we'll stop here for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I need, Excellency, 15 to 20 minutes, at least, at the minimum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Zepinic, we need to continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. But before doing so I have a couple of matters. The Chamber received a filing from the counsel for Mr. Naser Oric requesting for leave to respond to the Defence's second motion for subpoena. I wonder whether the parties have any observation to make about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We would ask that you grant leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm -- I don't have any position on it at the moment, but I haven't really been seized of that directly. If you could give us ten minutes to get back to -- I suspect there won't be a problem with that, but I'd rather check with anybody who has looked specifically at the request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And in terms of witness schedule, do we have a sufficient number of witnesses for this week, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will be going into Friday, but I'm not sure we will have enough witnesses to complete the whole of Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no witness to fill up?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a witness that's coming Thursday night but he would have to testify without being proofed. Last time we did that, it didn't work out very well, so we would prefer not to. But if you insisted, we could probably try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's see how it evolves. Please have a nice evening, Dr. Zepinic. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 14th day of February, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
